observation.visible_scene: A flooded cypress wetland: green ferns and reddish-brown cypress knees rise from dark shallow water in the foreground, with a row of tall, bare tree trunks receding into the background under an overcast sky. A 'WINYEDA' / 'SAMPLE' watermark sits at the right. People are present in the background among the trees throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: A cross-dissolve edit (not physical motion) blends two camera views of the same wetland: an early view dominated by opaque foreground ferns dissolves into a later, more open-water view in which those ferns become translucent/ghostly and the water surface with cypress knees and tree reflections becomes dominant (roughly t=0.13 to t=1.5).
In the first view, background figures — one bent over at the left and two standing close together near a tree at the right — are visible at the start and fade out as the dissolve progresses.
In the second (post-dissolve) view, a single person stays crouched beside the central tree trunk for the remainder of the clip.

A person in dark clothing walks across the background from left to right between about t=1.87 and t=2.34, passing behind the central tree (briefly occluded) and continuing toward the right side before leaving the visible area.
The water surface shows continuously shifting reflections of the sky and trunks.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the background people were doing before the clip and after it ends.
Whether the two dissolved views share the same camera position or differ in framing/height.
The reason for the editing cut and the identities/roles of the people.
uncertain_details: The exact count of background figures during the dissolve, since they overlap and fade.
Whether there is any slight camera pan or zoom in addition to the dissolve (background evidence is ambiguous).
The precise moment the walking person disappears, as occlusion by the tree and distance make tracking uncertain.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
